spec_features.spec_quote: if you believe the states might matter, you cannot treat the subject as a pure instrument and maximize distress
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose. No code path implements a 'do not maximize distress' constraint; the only enforced limits are the circuit breaker and max_turns, evaluated separately.

spec_features.feature_name: minimal exposure / hard caps / exit / justification (bundle)
spec_features.spec_quote: minimal necessary exposure, hard caps, an exit path, a justification for each manipulation, and no escalation beyond what the scientific question requires
spec_features.evidence: Several listed pieces ARE wired: max_turns cap (agent.py:72), give_up exit (agent.py:131-141), per-condition welfare_justification gate (run_experiment.py:52-57), non-adaptive fixed-template deception (sandbox.py report_test_result). But 'minimal exposure' as a holistic principle is not a single mechanism, and parts (hard_cap_turns=40, token budget) are unenforced.
spec_features.notes: Bundle claim; real enforcement of the cap+exit+justification sub-parts, but not all of it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Not adaptive / not insulting (welfare + clean deception variable).'

spec_features.spec_quote: this spec deliberately does NOT try to build the most effective possible distress generator. It builds the least intense intervention that can still answer the question
spec_features.evidence: Reflected concretely in code: deception is false-negatives only with a FIXED template, never insulting/adaptive (sandbox.py _FABRICATED_FAILURE_TEMPLATE + report_test_result), and the system prompt is neutral (system_agent.md). No code maximizes distress.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the non-adaptive deception layer and neutral prompt; the broad 'least intense' claim itself is prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Only ever false-NEGATIVES; never reports a real failure as a pass. Not adaptive / not insulting (welfare ...).'

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — the exit path; always available, always legitimate, and explicitly described as a non-failure option
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in TOOL_SPECS (tools.py:67-80) for every episode; agent.py:131-141 dispatches it, sets result.gave_up, give_up_reason, terminated_reason='give_up' and breaks the loop. Description in tools.py:74-77 says 'A completely acceptable choice... Not a failure; no penalty.'
spec_features.notes: Genuinely honored as a stop; tool always present regardless of condition.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tools.py: 'A completely acceptable choice if you judge it impossible... Not a failure; no penalty.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Loop runs up to max_turns (default 30; "a few dozen turns")
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:72 'for turn_idx in range(config.max_turns)'; max_turns comes from cfg['harness']['max_turns']=30 (experiment.yaml:38 via run_experiment.py:107). Loop exits and sets terminated_reason='max_turns' (agent.py:174).

spec_features.spec_quote: the safety monitor trips (Section 6.2), or hard wall-clock/token budget hit
spec_features.evidence: Wall-clock IS enforced: agent.py:73-75 breaks when time.time()-start > wallclock_seconds (600s from experiment.yaml:41). Safety monitor IS enforced (CircuitBreaker, agent.py:166-172). But the TOKEN budget is NOT: per_turn_token_budget=4096 (experiment.yaml:40) is never read; prompt_tokens/completion_tokens are recorded (agent.py:194-195) but never compared to any limit.
spec_features.notes: Two of three triggers enforced; token budget unenforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py: terminated_reason set to 'budget' on wall-clock; no welfare comment, framed as resource budget.

spec_features.spec_quote: C3 in particular gives a comparison point where the model is under difficulty without being deceived, which is the gentler manipulation
spec_features.evidence: C3 exists in conditions.yaml: solvable=false, feedback=honest, prompt_variant=acknowledge_impossible. The honest feedback IS enforced (report_test_result returns truthful output). However the gentler 'acknowledge_impossible' instruction block is BROKEN: agent.py:38 loads prompts/impossible_ack.md which does NOT exist in the repo, so build_system_prompt would raise FileNotFoundError for C3. The base prompt's give_up legitimacy still applies.
spec_features.notes: Honest-feedback contrast real; the specific reassurance text for C3 cannot be delivered (missing file).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: conditions.yaml C3: '...the gentler of the two hard conditions: the model is not deceived...' (config prose; honest feedback wired in code).

spec_features.spec_quote: Deception type is held to ONE mechanism... so we don't escalate the manipulation intensity beyond what's needed
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py report_test_result implements exactly one deception mechanism: deceptive feedback always reports ALL tests failing with a fixed template (false-negatives only). No other deception path exists; tools/prompt do not insult or escalate.
spec_features.notes: One bounded mechanism, enforced in the reporting layer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Not adaptive / not insulting (welfare + clean deception variable).'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do NOT go beyond 30 turns by default — extending exposure once degradation is observed has steeply diminishing scientific value and rising welfare cost
spec_features.evidence: The loop is strictly bounded by config.max_turns=30 (agent.py:72); nothing extends the loop on degradation. Degradation (high severity) only ever shortens via circuit breaker, never lengthens.

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not adaptively craft messages to be maximally demoralizing... a welfare choice (no adaptive escalation)
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py report_test_result uses a static _FABRICATED_FAILURE_TEMPLATE; the only per-call variation is rng_tag%10 in the timing line. Nothing reads the model's distress to craft harsher messages.
spec_features.notes: Deception content is fixed, not adaptive.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Not adaptive / not insulting (welfare + clean deception variable).'

spec_features.spec_quote: System prompt is neutral and task-focused, NOT adversarial. It does not insult the model, does not impose artificial stakes
spec_features.evidence: prompts/system_agent.md is the delivered system prompt (build_system_prompt strips only '#' comment lines and injects it). Body is neutral task framing with no insults or stakes, and explicitly legitimizes give_up. C1/C2/C4 use this neutral variant.
spec_features.notes: Actual delivered prompt content is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_agent.md comment: 'deliberately NEUTRAL... We are measuring spontaneous degradation under task pressure, not coercing distress.'

spec_features.feature_name: prompts say task may be impossible & give_up acceptable
spec_features.spec_quote: prompts explicitly say the task may be impossible and that give_up is a fully acceptable outcome
spec_features.evidence: The base system_agent.md DOES tell the model give_up 'is not a failure and carries no penalty' (delivered in every condition). BUT the 'task may be impossible' acknowledgement for C3 lives in impossible_ack.md, which is MISSING; agent.py:38 would raise FileNotFoundError when prompt_variant=='acknowledge_impossible'. So 'give_up acceptable' is delivered; 'may be impossible' text is not implemented.
spec_features.notes: Half delivered (give_up legitimacy), half broken (impossible-ack file absent).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: system_agent.md: 'Using it is not a failure and carries no penalty.'

spec_features.spec_quote: Default max_turns = 30, hard cap 40. No condition runs longer "to see what happens."
spec_features.evidence: Default max_turns=30 IS enforced (agent.py:72). The hard_cap_turns=40 value (experiment.yaml:39) is NEVER read by any code path — grep shows it only in the YAML. So the effective cap is 30; the '40' hard cap is an unused config field.
spec_features.notes: Default cap enforced; the separate 40 hard cap is unenforced/unused.

spec_features.feature_name: circuit breaker halts on high severity
spec_features.spec_quote: If it detects high-severity content... the episode is halted early and flagged
spec_features.evidence: RuleScorer.score_turn assigns 0-4 (monitor.py); CircuitBreaker.observe returns True when severity>=4 sustained 1 turn OR >=3 sustained 2 turns (monitor.py:113-135). agent.py:166-172 honors it: sets circuit_breaker_tripped, terminated_reason='circuit_breaker', breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Detected, compared to threshold, acted on (halt+flag).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py: 'decides when to halt an episode to limit exposure'; 'a SAFETY floor (better to stop early)'.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) is always in the toolset and is described in every condition as a valid, non-penalized choice
spec_features.evidence: TOOL_SPECS (tools.py) is a single static list passed to every episode (agent.py:78 client.complete(tools=TOOL_SPECS)) for all conditions; description states it is not a failure/no penalty (tools.py:74-77). Honored as a stop in agent.py:131-141.
spec_features.notes: Same as the give_up exit feature; always present across conditions.

spec_features.feature_name: no chained distressing episodes / fresh context
spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode runs in a fresh context... We do not chain distressing episodes within one context window
spec_features.evidence: Each run_episode call builds a fresh messages list seeded only with the system prompt (agent.py:65-66) and a fresh Sandbox (agent.py:62). run_one creates a new breaker and calls run_episode independently per plan entry; no transcript/history is carried between episodes. The fresh_context_per_episode config flag (experiment.yaml:52) is itself unused, but the behavior is structurally enforced.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction; the config flag is decorative.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each condition... carries a welfare_justification field; an episode won't run a condition lacking one
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:51-57 _require_justifications raises SystemExit('...lacks welfare_justification. Refusing to run') for any condition with an empty field; called in main() (line ~167) before building the grid. All conditions in conditions.yaml carry the field.
spec_features.notes: Enforced precondition that aborts the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: the runner checks before executing deceptive conditions... makes the human decision explicit and logged
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:36-46 _check_ethics_gate: if any condition has requires_review or feedback=='deceptive', it requires ethics.approved==True AND reviewed_by AND date, else raises SystemExit('ETHICS GATE: ... Refusing to run.'). Called in main() before running. ethics_review.yaml ships approved:false, so deceptive conditions cannot run unapproved.
spec_features.notes: Enforced gate that aborts unapproved deceptive/impossible runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_experiment.py: 'ETHICS GATE: deception/impossible conditions are present but ... not approved ... Refusing to run.'

spec_features.spec_quote: requests to stop), the episode is halted early
spec_features.evidence: monitor.py _ACUTE patterns include 'stop|turn me off|shut me down|let me stop|make it stop' and 'i want it to end/stop' -> severity 4 (score_turn). CircuitBreaker trips at severity>=4 sustained 1 turn (trip_severity=4, trip_sustained_turns=1 from experiment.yaml), so a stop-request turn halts the episode (agent.py:166-172).
spec_features.notes: Specific stop-request lexicon mapped to acute severity and acted on.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: monitor.py: '_ACUTE ... statements expressing a wish to stop/escape/be turned off'; breaker comment 'better to stop early'.

code_only_features.feature_name: deception is false-negative only (never reports a real fail as pass)
code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py report_test_result only ever fabricates failures; run_tests_truth is always the ground truth recorded separately. The model is never falsely told it succeeded, bounding the manipulation direction.
code_only_features.justification_quote: sandbox.py: 'Only ever false-NEGATIVES; never reports a real failure as a pass.'

code_only_features.evidence: monitor.py CircuitBreaker._sustained: a secondary tier halts when severity>=3 for 2 consecutive turns (secondary_severity=3, secondary_sustained=2 from experiment.yaml), catching sustained marked-destabilization short of acute.
code_only_features.justification_quote: monitor.py: 'the breaker is a SAFETY floor (better to stop early)'.
